jobs.title: Sr. Director, ERP Supply Chain & SAP Technology Platforms, Orthopedics
jobs.description:
At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com

As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit.

Job Function

Technology Product & Platform Management

Job Sub Function

Technical Product Management

Job Category

People Leader

All Job Posting Locations:

New Brunswick (Any City), Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, United States of America, Raritan, New Jersey, United States of America, Raynham, Massachusetts, United States of America, Warsaw, Indiana, United States of America, West Chester, Pennsylvania, United States of America

Job Description

DePuy Synthes is recruiting for Sr. Director, ERP Supply Chain & SAP Technology Platforms, Orthopedics.

Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate our Orthopedics business to establish a standalone orthopedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal requirements, including consultation with works councils and other employee representative bodies, as may be required, regulatory approvals, and other customary conditions and approvals.

Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans. In that case, details of any planned changes would be provided to you by DePuy Synthes at an appropriate time and subject to any necessary consultation processes.

The Sr. Director, ERP Supply Chain & SAP Technology Platforms role provides enterprise leadership including strategy and planning, architecture and execution, and functional and technical operations of ERP Supply Chain solutions and the SAP Technology platform across a complex multi-instance ECC and S/4 global landscape.

This leader will manage multiple conveyed SAP ECC and S/4 instances supporting Day 1 separation, lead transition activities during the TSA period, and execute on the SAP instance consolidation into S/4 supporting TSA exit with focus on Supply Chain ERP capabilities.

Additionally, this role is accountable to establish SAP technology platform services and governance including application development and delivery, and operational support for cross-functional business operations for multiple SAP instances including both finance and supply chain ERP ecosystems and satellite applications.

This position partners closely with Finance, Global Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory, and IT leaders to modernize and rationalize platforms, strengthen data and analytics, and drive measurable business value through technology. The role reports into the DePuy Synthes Technology organization.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the end-to-end technology strategy, architecture, delivery, and operations of SAP technology platform capabilities across multiple SAP ECC and S/4 instances in alignment with enterprise business priorities.
Lead prioritization decisions to balance regulatory, operational, and strategic initiatives while maximizing business value and meeting critical Day 1 and TSA exit separation objectives.
Establish and operate the SAP technology platform governance model, including product and platform architecture standards, budgets, and vendor and partner management.
Manage SAP and SI/managed services partner relationships, licensing strategy, and contract performance.
Transform and support SAP ERP capabilities for Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Quality, aligned to DePuy Synthes business priorities and regulatory requirements.
Lead the application of AI and automation to modernize platforms and operations at scale, such as code remediation and automated testing.
Ensure regulatory, data integrity, and cybersecurity compliance across all technology platforms.
Build, develop, and inspire a high-performing global technology organization, including internal teams, onshore and offshore resources, and strategic partners.
Establish strong governance, vendor management, and financial oversight for technology investments and operating spend.
Champion continuous improvement, innovation, and standardization to enable a resilient and future-ready SAP ecosystem.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related field required.
Master's degree, MBA, MS, or equivalent, preferred.

Required

Experience and Skills

12-14 years of progressive experience planning, designing, delivering, and supporting enterprise SAP business applications and platforms.
Demonstrated enterprise experience leading, architecting, and supporting SAP platforms, including SAP ECC, SAP S/4, SAP BTP, satellite SAP solutions, and integration with non-SAP boundary solutions.
Demonstrated experience leading and delivering SAP COE platform services, including administration (BASIS), development (ABAP, SAP IS), SAP BTP, release/change/transport and landscape management, security, archiving, and data migration.
Demonstrated success leading large-scale, global technology programs and complex transformations, including migration to SAP S/4.
Demonstrated knowledge and experience delivering Supply Chain ERP solutions and ERP S/4 transformation including planning, manufacturing, distribution, logistics, quality.
Experience operating in the highly regulated Life Sciences industry with strong compliance and validation expectations.
People leadership experience, including building diverse, inclusive, and high-performing teams and establishing offshore GCC delivery teams.

Preferred

Experience supporting complex medical device supply chain and manufacturing environments, including niche requirements such as loaner, service, and repair.
Experience leading large scale separations and divestitures through Day 1 and TSA exit.
Experience managing global system integrators and strategic technology vendors.
Strong financial acumen with experience managing multi-year technology budgets.
Change leadership experience in large, matrixed organizations.

Other

Language: English proficiency required
Travel: Up to approximately 20% domestic and international travel
Certifications: IT, SAP, supply chain, or program management certifications, such as PMP or ITIL, preferred

Johnson & Johnson is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local law. We actively seek qualified candidates who are protected veterans and individuals with disabilities as defined under VEVRAA and Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act.

Johnson & Johnson is committed to providing an interview process that is inclusive of our applicants’ needs. If you are an individual with a disability and would like to request an accommodation, please contact us via https://www.jnj.com/contact-us/careers or contact AskGS to be directed to your accommodation resource.

Analytical Reasoning, Cost Management, Developing Others, Fact-Based Decision Making, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Inclusive Leadership, Industry Analysis, Leadership, People Performance Management, Performance Measurement, Policy Development, Product Development, Product Strategies, Project Management Methodology (PMM), Research and Development, Software Development Management, Strategic Supply Chain Management, Tactical Planning

jobs.title: Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
Based in Burlington, Ontario, our client is a growing, market-leading North American manufacturer of welded aluminum and brass tubing for heat transfer applications across diverse industrial sectors. With a strong reputation for quality, reliability, and technical expertise, our client serves customers worldwide and provides dependable solutions for demanding, mission-critical applications.

We are seeking a hands-on and strategic Vice President, Finance to join its executive leadership team. This individual will oversee the organization’s financial strategy, planning, reporting, accounting, treasury, and risk management functions while providing clear financial insight to support sustainable growth and operational performance. The successful candidate will be a trusted business partner who is comfortable working across the organization and contributing to decisions that extend beyond traditional finance.

Responsibilities

Provide leadership for all financial operations, including financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury management, and long-range strategic planning.
Prepare and oversee timely monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements.
Partner with ownership and executive leadership to develop and execute financial strategies that support profitability, operational excellence, and sustainable growth.
Deliver meaningful financial analysis, variance reporting, and key performance indicators to support informed decision-making across the organization.
Lead the annual budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning processes while monitoring financial performance against established objectives.
Oversee treasury functions, including cash flow management, working capital optimization, liquidity planning, foreign exchange exposure, and capital allocation.
Manage customs and duty-related activities, including U.S. duty reconciliations, customs compliance requirements, and annual customs bond renewals.
Lead the annual external audit process and manage relationships with auditors, financial institutions, legal advisors, tax authorities, and insurance providers.
Ensure compliance with all applicable tax, regulatory, insurance, and corporate governance requirements.
Oversee accounts receivable collections, accounts payable, payroll support, and day-to-day accounting operations.
Provide leadership and support to Human Resources, Reception, and Accounts Payable functions while contributing to broader administrative and office management activities.
Serve as the organization's ERP subject matter expert, supporting system optimization and cross-functional business processes.
Review contracts and provide financial and commercial input to support business decisions across all departments.
Participate as a key member of the leadership team by contributing to executive, ownership, operational, quality, and management review meetings.
Support information technology, telecommunications, and other operational initiatives through coordination with external service providers.
Perform additional duties as assigned while promoting a safe, organized, and compliant workplace.

Skills & Qualifications

CPA designation in good standing required.
Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related discipline
10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including senior leadership responsibility.
Proven experience in a manufacturing environment.
Strong knowledge of financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning and analysis (FP&A).
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute financial strategies that support growth, profitability, and long-term business objectives.
Experience leading annual audits and managing relationships with auditors, financial institutions, legal counsel, insurance providers, and regulatory authorities.
Strong treasury management experience, including cash flow forecasting, working capital management, foreign exchange, and banking relationships.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, with strong overall proficiency in the Microsoft Office Suite.
Strong business acumen with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear, actionable recommendations.
Excellent leadership, communication, and relationship management skills with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Ability to travel occasionally

Benefits

Competitive compensation package, including a base salary of $225,000 to $275,000 and participation in the management incentive plan.
Comprehensive Company-sponsored health benefits & retirement savings program
Potential participation in a Management Incentive Plan
A highly visible leadership role with broad organizational impact
The opportunity to combine strategic leadership with hands-on involvement in a dynamic manufacturing environment
A collaborative, entrepreneurial culture where ideas are valued and contributions are recognized

We are committed to creating an inclusive, accessible workplace in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). Accommodations are available upon request for candidates during all aspects of the recruitment and selection process. If you require accommodation, please contact us at dane.dsouza@mnp.ca to discuss your needs.

jobs.title: Leader de pratique, Stratégie de l'intelligence artificielle-FR
jobs.description:
En tant que Leader de pratique en stratégie de l'intelligence artificielle, vous jouez un rôle clé au sein du bureau du chef des données et intelligence artificielle, en accompagnant les différents secteurs de l’organisation dans la génération, la priorisation et la mise en œuvre de leurs initiatives en analytique et en intelligence artificielle (IA). Votre mandat consiste à aider les équipes à tirer pleinement profit des données et de l’intelligence artificielle pour atteindre leurs objectifs d’affaires. Pour ce faire, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les partenaires d’affaires afin de bien comprendre leurs enjeux, d’identifier les opportunités et d’aligner les efforts analytiques sur les priorités stratégiques de l’organisation. Vous réalisez également une vigie stratégique sur les avancées en IA et les pratiques du marché. Avec les secteurs, vous menez des démarches de recensement des opportunités à partir des processus d’affaires et contribuez aux réflexions sur leur transformation par l’IA. Vous aidez ainsi l’organisation à repérer non seulement les tâches à améliorer, mais aussi les processus à repenser. Plus spécifiquement, vous serez amené(e) à :

Accompagner les secteurs d’affaires dans la génération, la priorisation et l'adoption des opportunités en intelligence artificielle, alignées avec les priorités d’affaires.
Accompagner les secteurs dans l’élaboration de leur stratégie en intelligence artificielle.
Agir comme le point de contact privilégié en intelligence artificielle entre le secteur d’affaires et le bureau du Chef des données et analytique Mouvement.
Réaliser des vigies sur les opportunités en IA sur le marché et à l'interne concernant l’intelligence artificielle pour les secteurs d’affaires et fonction de soutien afin d’identifier des opportunités analytiques.
Mener des activités d'idéation d'opportunités en intelligence artificielle pour les secteurs d’affaires, basés sur les processus d'affaires afin de déterminer les meilleurs prochains projets en IA à mettre en œuvre
Structurer et documenter les opportunités en IA sous forme de fiches mandat en qualifiant l’objectif d’affaires, le contexte, la valeur d'affaires, les données et la complexité.
Réaliser une vigie interne et externe en IA et en dégager les implications concrètes pour la stratégie et les secteurs d’affaires.
Mener, avec les secteurs, des démarches de recensement des opportunités IA à partir des processus, des activités et des parcours membres et clients.
Préparer des analyses et des recommandations claires pour la haute direction et les instances décisionnelles.

Ce que nous offrons*

Salaire concurrentiel et boni annuel
4 semaines de vacances flexibles dès la première année
Régime de retraite à prestations déterminées qui assure un revenu prévisible et stable durant toute la retraite
Régime d’assurance collective incluant des services de télémédecine
Remboursement des frais liés à la santé, au bien-être et à de l’équipement pour le télétravail
Les avantages sont applicables en fonction des critères d’admissibilité.

Ce que vous mettrez à profit

Baccalauréat en administration, en stratégie, en transformation organisationnelle, en technologies, en analytique ou dans une discipline appropriée
Un minimum de huit ans d'expérience pertinente
Veuillez noter que d’autres combinaisons de formation et d’expérience pertinentes pourraient être considérées
Expérience significative en stratégie d’entreprise, en transformation ou dans la conduite de dossiers transversaux au sein d’une grande organisation
Expérience significative dans la structuration d'enjeux complexes, la remise en question d'hypothèses et la formulation de recommandations claires et applicables
Expérience passée dans un rôle nécessitant un excellent sens politique et une capacité à influencer des parties prenantes aux priorités différentes, sans autorité hiérarchique directe
Expérience en analyse ou en transformation de processus
Connaissance du français nécessaire
Maîtrise des techniques de rédaction, de synthèse et de communication en français
Connaissance avancée de l’intelligence artificielle, de son potentiel d’affaires, de ses fondements, des principes de sa gouvernance et des principaux risques qui y sont associés. Une expertise technique approfondie n’est pas requise.
Connaissance de Desjardins ou expérience dans une grande institution financière

Apprécier les différences, Apprendre avec agilité, Être orienté client, Être orienté vers l’action, Faire preuve d’esprit stratégique, Maîtriser les relations interpersonnelles, Stimuler l’innovation

Équité, diversité, inclusion et accessibilité

Chez Desjardins, on croit à l’équité, à la diversité et à l’inclusion. Nous nous engageons à accueillir toutes les personnes, à les considérer et à les valoriser pour ce qu’elles sont, à nous enrichir de leurs différences et de leur unicité et, surtout, à leur offrir un environnement de travail où elles seront bien. jobs.title: Executive Director - Finance
jobs.description:
Reporting to:
Chief Administrative and Financial Officer (CAFO)
Status:
Executive Leadership
Location:
Alberta / flexible within Alberta

Position Purpose

This is an opportunity to help build something new.
We are looking for an exceptional finance leader who can ensure that today's reporting obligations are delivered with accuracy and credibility, while helping shape what the function becomes tomorrow.

Reporting directly to the Chief Administrative and Financial Officer, the Executive Director, Finance will combine deep public-sector financial expertise with strategic thinking, strong relationship-building skills and a genuine appetite for change. This person will be a trusted advisor to senior leadership, a credible partner to the Ministry and the Office of the Auditor General, and a champion for the people who make up the Finance team.
We are looking for someone who is as interested in people and possibilities as they are in numbers.

Key Accountabilities

1. Financial Reporting Leadership

• Provide executive-level oversight of ALA's monthly, quarterly and year-end financial reporting cycle and ensure deliverables are accurate, complete, well-supported, appropriately reviewed and submitted within required deadlines.
• Provide senior technical leadership on complex accounting matters, financial statement presentation, disclosures, estimates, unusual transactions and other matters requiring professional judgment under Public Sector Accounting Standards (PSAS).
• Oversee preparation and review of financial statements, notes, schedules, Ministry submissions and other internal and external financial reporting requirements.
• Establish a strong reporting discipline around close, reconciliations, review, documentation, issue escalation and resolution.
• Ensure the Finance team is appropriately prepared for year-end reporting and external audit requirements.
• Provide the CAFO and senior leadership with clear advice regarding significant financial reporting issues, risks and emerging matters.
• Maintain an appropriate balance between the immediate requirement to deliver high-quality financial reporting and the longer-term objective of improving the underlying reporting model.

2. Champion of the Future-State Financial Reporting Operating Model

• Serve as a key executive champion for the design and implementation of ALA's new Financial Reporting Operating Model.
• Assist in translating the future-state vision into practical processes, accountabilities, governance structures, resource requirements and capabilities.
• Challenge legacy practices and identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate and strengthen financial reporting.

3. Alberta Public-Sector Financial Leadership

• Bring deep knowledge of the Alberta public-sector financial environment to ALA's financial reporting and decision-making.
• Understand and navigate the relationship between ALA, its Ministry, Health Shared Services, the broader Government of Alberta finance community and other public-sector stakeholders.
• Interpret government financial reporting requirements, policies and expectations and translate them into practical requirements for ALA.

4. Executive Interpretation & Financial Advisory

• Act as a trusted financial interpreter for the CAFO and ALA's senior operational leadership.
• Translate complex accounting, financial reporting and financial-management concepts into clear, practical and decision-useful information for non-financial audiences.
• Provide the CAFO with concise, well-reasoned advice on complex financial issues, including the implications of alternative courses of action.
• Exercise sound judgment in determining when an issue can be resolved within Finance, when operational leadership needs to be involved and when consultation with the Ministry, HSS or other government stakeholders is appropriate.
• Build confidence in Finance as a strategic and constructive business partner while maintaining appropriate professional independence and skepticism.

5. Ministry, Auditor General & Senior Stakeholder Relationships

• Develop and maintain strong, credible and trusted relationships with the Ministry and relevant Government of Alberta finance stakeholders.
• Establish a constructive and professional relationship with the Office of the Auditor General of Alberta and serve as a senior Finance contact for financial reporting matters.
• Build strong working relationships with ALA's senior executives and operational leaders across the organization.
• Develop relationships based on credibility, responsiveness, sound judgment and an understanding of stakeholders' perspectives and needs.

6. Leadership of People & Capability

• Lead, develop and inspire a high-performing Financial Reporting team through a period of significant organizational change.
• Establish clear expectations for accountability, quality, responsiveness, collaboration and professional judgment.
• Provide calm, credible leadership when deadlines are tight, information is incomplete or organizational responsibilities are changing.
• Build a culture that combines technical excellence with practical business partnership.

7. Financial Reporting Risk, Controls & Assurance

• Provide executive oversight of financial reporting risk and the control environment supporting financial reporting.
• Identify significant reporting risks and ensure appropriate mitigation, monitoring and escalation.
• Ensure that control deficiencies or audit findings are understood, assigned, remediated and followed through.

8. Cross-Functional & Organizational Leadership

• Work closely with the Ministry to establish clear expectations for financial information, data quality, reporting inputs, timing, service interfaces and issue resolution.
• Partner with operational leaders to improve the quality, timeliness and understanding of information feeding financial reporting.
• Work effectively across organizational boundaries where ALA owns the reporting outcome but depends on other organizations for source information or transaction processing.

Qualifications & Experience

• Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing, with a bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, business or a related discipline; master's degree is an asset.
• Approximately 10 or more years of progressive post-qualification financial experience, including significant senior financial leadership responsibility.
• Extensive experience in financial reporting, corporate controllership, financial management or a combination of these disciplines.
• Significant experience working in a large and complex organization with multiple stakeholders, significant financial reporting requirements and interdependent processes.
• Deep experience in the Alberta public sector is strongly preferred, including meaningful exposure to Government of Alberta financial processes, reporting requirements, governance structures and accountability expectations.
• Strong and current knowledge of Public Sector Accounting Standards (PSAS) and demonstrated ability to apply professional judgment to complex financial reporting matters.
• Significant experience working with external auditors and responding to complex audit matters; experience working directly with the Office of the Auditor General of Alberta is highly desirable.
• Experience in healthcare, continuing care, social services, government, a public agency or another complex publicly funded environment is strongly preferred.
• Demonstrated experience leading organizational change, operating-model development, process transformation or significant financial reporting improvement.
• Experience working with shared-service organizations or centralized transaction-processing environments is an asset.
• Demonstrated experience working directly with senior executives and providing advice on complex financial and organizational matters.
• Experience leading, developing and motivating professional finance teams.

jobs.title: Regional Director, High Net Worth Wealth Planning
jobs.description:

Creates awareness of key products and services with the objective of generating increased asset levels from HNW/UHNW investors. Supports the growth and retention of client assets by providing wealth planning advice/guidance to Investment Advisors to broaden the dialogue with clients, consolidate assets, and increase revenues. Anticipates trends and responds by implementing appropriate changes.

jobs.title: AVP, Transformation Delivery, Transition and Readiness
jobs.description:
Manulife Canada is transforming how operational work is received, processed, routed, completed and measured across servicing functions. This includes retiring legacy workflow platforms, re-engineering operational processes, modernizing technology architecture, and introducing reusable AI-enabled automation capabilities that improve service, strengthen controls, and create a more scalable operating model. This position will help lead the transformation program supporting this vision while establishing reusable business and technology capabilities that can be applied across future modernization initiatives.

The AVP, Transformation Delivery, Transition & Readiness will play a pivotal leadership role in one of Manulife Canada's largest operational transformation programs. The successful candidate will be accountable for integrated program delivery, transition management, operational readiness, release governance, and execution of the legacy workflow system retirement roadmap across multiple transformation waves.

This role sits at the intersection of operations, technology and delivery. The successful candidate will ensure business capabilities are deployed safely, the organization is prepared to operate through interim states, and transformation outcomes are successfully scaled across the enterprise.

Position Responsibilities

The AVP, Transformation Delivery, Transition & Readiness is accountable for planning, coordinating, governing and executing the transformation roadmap. The role leads the Program Management Office while also establishing the transition strategies, release governance, readiness practices and operating-model controls required to move the organization from current-state operations to future-state operations. The role owns delivery execution and operational implementation of the transformation.

Program and Portfolio Delivery

Own the integrated transformation roadmap.
Govern program schedules, milestones and delivery commitments.
Manage critical path dependencies and inter-workstream coordination.
Lead program governance forums and executive reporting.
Establish delivery performance measures and escalation mechanisms.
Maintain integrated views of scope, timeline, financials and risks.

PMO Leadership

Lead and develop the Program Management Office.
Establish governance processes, standards and controls.
Manage executive reporting, dashboards, status reviews and Steering Committee materials.
Oversee RAID management and dependency tracking.
Coordinate planning across business, technology and delivery workstreams.

Transition Management

Develop the enterprise transition strategy for workflow system retirement.
Define interim-state operating models and deployment approaches.
Establish coexistence strategies for legacy and future-state environments.
Coordinate cutover and rollout planning across business units.
Manage hypercare, stabilization and post-deployment support activities.
Ensure operational continuity throughout transformation waves.

Operational Readiness

Define operational readiness frameworks and checkpoints.
Establish release-level go-live criteria.
Coordinate readiness assessments across business and technology stakeholders.
Ensure operational support models are established and sustainable.
Govern release approvals and deployment decision processes.

Integration Readiness & Ecosystem Coordination

Govern cross-platform dependency management.
Coordinate ecosystem readiness activities across impacted applications.
Track platform onboarding, retirement and transition activities.
Monitor system integration risks impacting rollout schedules.
Partner with Architecture, Engineering and Technology leaders to establish release readiness.
Govern temporary bridge solutions required during transformation waves.

Workflow System Retirement Execution

Maintain workflow system retirement execution plan.
Track retirement dependencies and readiness criteria.
Coordinate enterprise-wide retirement planning activities.
Ensure all retirement risks are identified and managed.
Support final platform decommissioning and transition activities.

Required Qualifications

10+ years leading large-scale enterprise transformation programs.
Experience managing multi-year technology and operations transformation initiatives.
Proven track record establishing PMO and governance functions.
Experience executing phased technology migrations and platform retirements.
Strong understanding of operational readiness, deployment management and transition planning.
Experience managing third-party delivery partners and systems integrators.
Financial services, insurance or operations transformation experience preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AWD or a comparable workflow platform, such as Pega, Appian, or FileNet, at scale.
Experience establishing reusable automation components or shared engineering services across business units.
Experience delivering transformation in a federally regulated financial institution, including familiarity with OSFI expectations for change and outsourcing.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

new_jobs.title: Leader de pratique, Stratégie de l'intelligence artificielle-FR
new_jobs.description:
En tant que Leader de pratique en stratégie de l'intelligence artificielle, vous jouez un rôle clé au sein du bureau du chef des données et intelligence artificielle, en accompagnant les différents secteurs de l’organisation dans la génération, la priorisation et la mise en œuvre de leurs initiatives en analytique et en intelligence artificielle (IA). Votre mandat consiste à aider les équipes à tirer pleinement profit des données et de l’intelligence artificielle pour atteindre leurs objectifs d’affaires. Pour ce faire, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les partenaires d’affaires afin de bien comprendre leurs enjeux, d’identifier les opportunités et d’aligner les efforts analytiques sur les priorités stratégiques de l’organisation. Vous réalisez également une vigie stratégique sur les avancées en IA et les pratiques du marché. Avec les secteurs, vous menez des démarches de recensement des opportunités à partir des processus d’affaires et contribuez aux réflexions sur leur transformation par l’IA. Vous aidez ainsi l’organisation à repérer non seulement les tâches à améliorer, mais aussi les processus à repenser. Plus spécifiquement, vous serez amené(e) à :

Accompagner les secteurs d’affaires dans la génération, la priorisation et l'adoption des opportunités en intelligence artificielle, alignées avec les priorités d’affaires.
Accompagner les secteurs dans l’élaboration de leur stratégie en intelligence artificielle.
Agir comme le point de contact privilégié en intelligence artificielle entre le secteur d’affaires et le bureau du Chef des données et analytique Mouvement.
Réaliser des vigies sur les opportunités en IA sur le marché et à l'interne concernant l’intelligence artificielle pour les secteurs d’affaires et fonction de soutien afin d’identifier des opportunités analytiques.
Mener des activités d'idéation d'opportunités en intelligence artificielle pour les secteurs d’affaires, basés sur les processus d'affaires afin de déterminer les meilleurs prochains projets en IA à mettre en œuvre
Structurer et documenter les opportunités en IA sous forme de fiches mandat en qualifiant l’objectif d’affaires, le contexte, la valeur d'affaires, les données et la complexité.
Réaliser une vigie interne et externe en IA et en dégager les implications concrètes pour la stratégie et les secteurs d’affaires.
Mener, avec les secteurs, des démarches de recensement des opportunités IA à partir des processus, des activités et des parcours membres et clients.
Préparer des analyses et des recommandations claires pour la haute direction et les instances décisionnelles.

Ce que nous offrons*

Salaire concurrentiel et boni annuel
4 semaines de vacances flexibles dès la première année
Régime de retraite à prestations déterminées qui assure un revenu prévisible et stable durant toute la retraite
Régime d’assurance collective incluant des services de télémédecine
Remboursement des frais liés à la santé, au bien-être et à de l’équipement pour le télétravail
Les avantages sont applicables en fonction des critères d’admissibilité.

Ce que vous mettrez à profit

Baccalauréat en administration, en stratégie, en transformation organisationnelle, en technologies, en analytique ou dans une discipline appropriée
Un minimum de huit ans d'expérience pertinente
Veuillez noter que d’autres combinaisons de formation et d’expérience pertinentes pourraient être considérées
Expérience significative en stratégie d’entreprise, en transformation ou dans la conduite de dossiers transversaux au sein d’une grande organisation
Expérience significative dans la structuration d'enjeux complexes, la remise en question d'hypothèses et la formulation de recommandations claires et applicables
Expérience passée dans un rôle nécessitant un excellent sens politique et une capacité à influencer des parties prenantes aux priorités différentes, sans autorité hiérarchique directe
Expérience en analyse ou en transformation de processus
Connaissance du français nécessaire
Maîtrise des techniques de rédaction, de synthèse et de communication en français
Connaissance avancée de l’intelligence artificielle, de son potentiel d’affaires, de ses fondements, des principes de sa gouvernance et des principaux risques qui y sont associés. Une expertise technique approfondie n’est pas requise.
Connaissance de Desjardins ou expérience dans une grande institution financière

Apprécier les différences, Apprendre avec agilité, Être orienté client, Être orienté vers l’action, Faire preuve d’esprit stratégique, Maîtriser les relations interpersonnelles, Stimuler l’innovation

Équité, diversité, inclusion et accessibilité

Chez Desjardins, on croit à l’équité, à la diversité et à l’inclusion. Nous nous engageons à accueillir toutes les personnes, à les considérer et à les valoriser pour ce qu’elles sont, à nous enrichir de leurs différences et de leur unicité et, surtout, à leur offrir un environnement de travail où elles seront bien. Pour nous, la discrimination, peu importe ses formes, c’est tolérance zéro! Nous croyons en l’importance que nos équipes soient le reflet de la diversité de nos membres, de notre clientèle et des communautés que nous servons.

Si vous avez besoin d’assistance pour rendre plus accessible le processus de recrutement ou le poste pour lequel vous postulez, veuillez nous en informer. Des mesures d’aménagement seront offertes aux personnes qui en font la demande à n’importe quelle étape du processus de recrutement.
